rows: Bi Sheng, China, ~1040 CE — ceramic. Korean bronze type ~1230s. Gutenberg ~1450.
1377 Korean book — oldest surviving metal movable-type printed book. Now in Paris.
Why didn't East Asian movable type transform society?
Multi-factor: 5,000-50,000 character set, woodblock printing already mature, different economic model, state/religious control
Wooden type system (~1298), revolving type cases for large character set, first systematic documentation
Digital computing: Unicode encoding + phonetic input methods + software-driven character selection
How many characters does Chinese require?
Basic literacy: ~3,000. Scholarly: ~10,000. Complete: ~50,000+. Compare Latin: ~100 type pieces.
Why did woodblock persist in Japan?
Aesthetic (cursive brush strokes), illustration integration, and woodblock often faster for reprinting same text
Korean phonetic alphabet (1443 CE), ~40 elements vs 50,000 Chinese characters; not widely used for printing until 20th c.
